Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
Condition : 2 - The proposed development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in the application and the plans and supporting documents submitted there with (insert numbers/references) and approved by the Local Planning Authority, or as shall have been otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the building is used.
Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission. 
Condition : 3 - No development above ground level shall take place on any Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan) hereby permitted until full details and samples of materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of that Relevant Building have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details must include a detailed schedule of materials, a photographic sample board and rendered drawings, elevations and sections at a sufficient scale (1:20 or 1:50) to illustrate how all external materials will appear together.
The samples/details shall include: 
(a)	Brick/stonework (including brick, stone, masonry, brick panels, feature brick panel, brick framing feature and mortar on-site sample panel, minimum one metre by one metre) including all mortar colours, joint type, brick bond and a brick and mortar onsite sample panel (min. 2m x 2m);
(b)	Cladding materials / render (including system specifications and on-site samples where relevant);
(c)	Samples and details of all externally visible car park materials;
(d)	Roof coverings; including materials, parapet coping / capping materials, dormers and canopies;
(e)	Window, door and roller shutter types and treatments; and sectional drawings of reveals / sills / head details 
(f)	Balustrading and handrail treatments, including to roof areas (including details / sections / materials of soffits, panels and frames); 
(g)	Any other materials / details / fittings to be used (including solar panels, extract vents, rainwater goods, boiler flues etc.), with sections and on-site samples where appropriate
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter. 
Reason:  In order to safeguard the visual amenity of the area and buildings.
Condition : 4 - No development above ground level shall take place until full and finalised details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include:  
- a statement setting out the design objectives and how these will be delivered; 
- an implementation programme (including phasing of work where relevant); and
- plans and written specifications of all soft landscaping works, including any grass and turf areas, trees, planters, shrub and herbaceous areas, noting details of species, sizes, numbers / densities and any associated cultivation / relevant operations;
- a 'Tree Planting Statement' providing full details, locations, specifications and construction methods for all purpose-built tree pits and associated above ground features, including specifications for tree protection and a stated volume of suitable growing medium to facilitate and promote the healthy development of the proposed trees, ensuring each tree has a soil volume equivalent of 0.6 times its canopy area at maturity;
- existing and proposed finished levels or contours; 
- proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (e.g. drainage, power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating alignments, levels, access points, supports as relevant); 
- hard landscaping proposals, including ground surface materials, kerbs, edges, ridge and flexible paving, refuse disposal points and if applicable synthetic surfaces for both ground level and roof terrace level (where relevant);
- fences, walls and any other boundary treatments/retaining structures;
- vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas;
- any signage and information boards, in addition to artwork/ wayfinding/sculptural features; 
- any brown and/or green roofs; 
- any CCTV equipment; 
- any other landscaping feature(s) forming part of the scheme. 
The submission shall include a management programme for the lifetime of the developm
Condition : 5 - Prior to first occupation of the refurbished Gillette building, new Sounds Stages or new Multi-Storey Car Park (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), full details of all boundary treatment, gates and barriers for the proposed development shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall indicate the positions, heights, design, materials and type of boundary treatment, gates and barriers to be erected, and the development shall be carried out in accordance with these details, and retained thereafter.  
Reason: In order to minimise danger, obstruction and inconvenience to users of the highway and of the access.
Condition : 6 - Prior to first occupation of the refurbished Gillette building, new Sounds Stages or new Multi-Storey Car Park (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), and notwithstanding any details in the submitted plans, full details of all external lighting for the proposed development shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority as part of a lighting strategy and plan, which shall also include details of any illuminated signage facing the public highway. The approved details shall indicate the positions, heights, design, lighting output/ specifications and types of lighting fixtures to be installed, and all lighting shall be carried out and maintained in accordance with these approved details for the lifetime of the development.
Artificial lighting as part of the completed development shall be designed to meet the Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior Lighting Installations for Environmental Zone - E2 set out in Table 2 of the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, 01/21  (https://theilp.org.uk/publication/guidance-note-1-for-the-reduction-of-obtrusive-light-2021/)  or such other guidance as may supersede it.  The installation shall be examined by a lighting engineer affiliated to a nationally recognised body that specialises in the field of external lighting and certified to confirm that it complies with this standard before it is first brought into use and a copy of the certificate supplied to the Local Planning Authority to confirm compliance before the lights are first brought into operation. Where possible, use of low UV warm-white LED bulbs with directional, downward facing and shielded lights for sections is encouraged, especially adjacent to sensitive receptors (e.g. residential dwellings). Internal luminaires can be recessed where installed in proximity to windows to reduce glare and light spill or treated with low tran
Condition : 7 - Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), details (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, to demonstrate that that the works to the Relevant Building have been carried out in accordance with the following sustainable sourcing of materials requirements:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- 	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme. 
- 	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.
Condition : 8 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the hereby approved Energy Statement (Rev 04) dated July 2024.
b)	Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that the Relevant Building has been constructed and finished in accordance with the approved Energy Statement to achieve a site-wide carbon reduction in emissions of 73% on Part L Building Regulations. 
c)	Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, suitable devices for the monitoring of the low and zero carbon technologies shall have been installed, and the monitored data shall be submitted automatically to a monitoring web-platform at daily intervals for a period of three years from the point of full operation.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 9 - Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), the post-construction tab of the GLA's whole life carbon assessment template should be completed accurately and in its entirety in line with the GLA's Whole Life Carbon Assessment Guidance for that Relevant Building and associated part of the site. The post-construction assessment should provide an update of the information submitted at planning submission stage, including the whole life carbon emission figures for all life-cycle modules based on the actual materials, products and systems used. This should be submitted to the GLA at: ZeroCarbonPlanning@london.gov.uk, along with any supporting evidence as per the guidance. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise on-site carbon dioxide savings.
Condition : 10 - Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) - P01 � Proposed Building Plan), a Post Completion Report for that Relevant Building and associated part of the site setting out the predicted and actual performance against all numerical targets in the relevant Circular Economy Statement shall be submitted to the GLA at: CircularEconomyLPG@london.gov.uk, along with any supporting evidence as per the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance. The Post Completion Report shall provide updated versions of Tables 1 and 2 of the Circular Economy Statement, the Recycling and Waste Reporting form and Bill of Materials. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  
Reason: In the interests of sustainable waste management and in order to maximise the re-use of materials.
Condition : 11 - Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), full details of the proposed heat pumps for that Relevant Building and associated part of the site shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These shall include:
-	An estimate of the heating and/or cooling energy (MWh/annum) the heat pumps would provide to the development and the percentage of contribution to the site's heat loads to demonstrate how the heat fraction from heat pump technologies has been maximised.
-	Details of the Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) and/or Seasonal Energy Efficiency ratio (SEER) and how these have been calculated including the expected heat source and heat distribution temperatures (for space heat and hot water) and the distribution loss factor, which shall be calculated based on the above information.
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards.
Condition : 12 - A. Prior to commencement of any above-ground development  (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) on any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), details of the specifications regarding power, number, appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority to show how the renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved and maximised for that Relevant Building and part of the site. The photovoltaic panels shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the relevant part of the development and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.
B. No solar panels shall be installed until a glint and glare assessment for the Relevant Building has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No subsequent alterations to the approved scheme are to take place unless submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards and to ensure the development does not endanger the safe movement of aircraft or the operation of Heathrow Airport. The airport requires a glint and glare assessment to be completed to determine the full impact on Air Traffic Control Tower and pilots approaching the airport.
Condition : 13 - (a) Within three months of commencement of any Relevant Building hereby permitted (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), a BREEAM Design Stage certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating will be achieved in accordance with approved documents for that Relevant Building and associated part of the site.
(b) Within six months of the date of first occupation of the Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), a BREEAM Post-Construction Review certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating has been achieved.
Reason: In order to ensure the highest standard of sustainable design and construction.
Supporting notes: 
Details submitted should state if BREEAM will be fully fitted, shell and core or shell only. Additional BREEAM Refurbishment and Fit-Out details will likely be required where not specified as fully fitted.
Condition : 14 - a) Prior to commencement of groundworks (except refurbishment of existing retained buildings, demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), the applicant shall have submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, in consultation with the Lead Local Flood Authority a final detailed drainage design including: relevant parts of the site as they relate to each Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan); drawings; supporting calculations; and an updated Drainage Assessment Form or SuDS Proforma. This shall all align with the Drainage Strategy (dated July 2024) and associated submissions hereby approved. All proposed SuDS features and the total site area should be incorporated into the calculations. It should be demonstrated that on-site flow as a result of the 1 in 100 year event with a climate change consideration must be suitably managed, with exceedance flows directed away from buildings. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. Consent from Thames Water for the proposed discharge connection must be provided, with details provided about how surface water discharge would take place. 
b) Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), evidence (photographs and installation contracts) shall have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the Relevant Building and associated part of the site has been completed in accordance with the details approved under part a) of this condition. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained permanently thereafter in accordance with the agree
Condition : 15 - No piling shall take place until a Piling Method Statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Thames Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement.
Reason: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility infrastructure. Piling has the potential to significantly impact / cause failure of local underground sewerage utility infrastructure. 
Supporting notes (from Thames Water):
Please read our guide 'working near our assets' to ensure your workings will be in line with the necessary processes you need to follow if you're considering working above or near our pipes or other structures. 
Should you require further information please contact Thames Water. Email: developer.services@thameswater.co.uk Phone: 0800 009 3921 (Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm) Write to: Thames Water Developer Services, Clearwater Court, Vastern Road, Reading, Berkshire RG1 8DB
Condition : 16 - Development shall be carried out in strict accordance with the provisions of Phase 1 Desk Study Report (Ref. CGE/16844, dated July 2023) hereby approved. 
If, during implementation of the measures set out in the Phase 1 report (e.g. through ground investigation), it becomes clear that ground gas monitoring or intrusive investigations are required, a Phase II site investigation report must be undertaken before any development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations commences. This report must be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work. 
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at
Condition : 17 - If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development (except refurbishment of existing buildings, demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the Local Planning Authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 18 - The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. 
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the Local Planning Authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 19 - The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented as part of the development. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation for relevant parts of the development by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval, before that part of the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
Condition : 20 - If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the Local Planning Authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice. 
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. 
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.
Condition : 21 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until an Inclusive Access Strategy for the Relevant Building and associated part of the site (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which shall include: details of the arrival, entrance and movement through the buildings ensuring a fully automated solution, and how any level changes around the site would be overcome. The approved details shall be implemented fully prior to first occupation of that Relevant Building and shall be retained as such thereafter. 
Reason: To provide a socially inclusive and sustainable development.
Condition : 22 - The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO). Prior to first occupation of any Relevant Building and associated part of the site (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), evidence of the accreditation achieved shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: To minimise opportunities for crime and to increase safety for residents and people in the locality.
Condition : 23 - Prior to the commencement of the development, including any demolition works, a detailed Ecological Management and Enhancement Strategy (EMES) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, for implementation alongside the provisions of the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (dated July 2024). The EMP shall incorporate:
i.	details of measures to protect breeding birds, nests and eggs from mortality/damage, injury and disturbance, including avoidance by timing and/or appropriate supervision, and a commitment to alert the LPA in the event of unexpected sightings of protected species during demolition and construction (including details of relevant protocol in such a scenario, in addition to the name and credentials of a qualified professional to oversee the works);
ii.	details of the ecological clerk of works supervision to be put in place to monitor the clearance of vegetation and other works affecting potential habitats to ensure no impact on undiscovered or other unexpected faunal encounters (i.e. toolbox talk with anyone involved with construction to make them aware of potential presence of bats, nesting birds and other protected species, and what to do in the event of an unexpected encounter)
iii.	details of careful working procedures;
iv.	specific provisions for the protection and enhancement of the peregrine falcon habitat identified at the site;
v.	an ecological lighting plan / strategy showing how lighting on site would be designed to avoid harm to existing and future ecology on site (e.g. light intensity and hours of use);
vi.	finalised details of ecological enhancement, including biodiversity net gains (plus supporting biometric calculations/ area habitat summary) and urban greening facto;
vii.	details of how the enhancement measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long-term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules (including annual work Plan for 30
Condition : 24 - Any removal of trees, hedgerows, shrubs, scrub or tall herbaceous vegetation shall be undertaken between September and February inclusive. If this is not possible then a suitably qualified ecologist shall check the areas concerned immediately prior to the clearance works to ensure that no nesting or nest-building birds are present. If any nesting birds are present, then the vegetation shall not be removed until the fledglings have left the nest. 
Reason: All wild birds, their nests and young are protected during the nesting period under The Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended). In the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity. 
Condition : 25 - Prior to the commencement of any Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01) � Proposed Building Plan), including any demolition works and site preparation, a Demolition Environmental Management Plan shall have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority for that Relevant Building and associated part of the site. The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the demolition period. The Plan shall include:
�	Site plan showing the position of the various elements required to support the demolition (welfare facilities, site hut/office);
�	Confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage caused;
�	Details of the parking for site operatives and visitors (to be indicated on the site plan);
�	Loading and storage areas for the excavated materials;
�	Proposed washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the council;
�	Measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access; Commitment to avoid attendance to the site by large vehicles (HGV) associated with the proposed works.
Reason. To ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved and in the interests of air quality and mitigating impacts on neighbouring premises.
Condition : 26 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein. 
The developer shall keep an up-to-date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/. 
Reason: In the interests of preventing harmful air quality impacts.
Condition : 27 - No development shall take place until a finalised and detailed Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) for the Relevant Building (as identified in plan reference GLT - GEN - ZZ - RF- D - A - 035200 (P01)  � Proposed Building Plan) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CEMP shall provide details of how demolition and construction works are to be undertaken and include:
The submitted Construction Method Statement shall include as a minimum detail of:
-	An identification of stages of works (including site preparation and construction stages); 
-	Details of working hours, which unless otherwise agreed with the Local Planning Authority shall be limited to 08.00 to 18.00 Monday to Friday and 08.00 to 13.00 on Saturdays); 
-	Procedures for maintaining good public relations including complaint management (logbook for complaints),  public consultation and liaison, all in compliance with British Standards BS 5228-1:2009+A1:2014 and best practicable means;
-	Mitigation measured as defined in BS 5228: Parts 1 and 2: 2009 Noise and Vibration Control on Construction and Open Sites shall be used to minimise noise disturbance from construction works (including noise mitigation measures for all plant and processors);
-	Measures to control emissions (including dust suppression and the need to contain stored or accumulated material so as to prevent it becoming airborne at any time) during the construction phase, in line with the requirements of the Mayor's Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, including the methods to be used and the measures to be undertaken to monitor and control the emission of dust, noise and vibration arising from construction works;
-	Details showing how all vehicles associated with the construction works are properly washed and cleaned to prevent the passage to mud and dirt onto the adjoining highway);
-	Details of provisions for recycling of materials, the provision 
Condition : 28 - No development above ground shall commence until a Bird Hazard Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted plan shall include details of:
- Management of any flat/shallow pitched/green roofs on buildings within the site which may be attractive to nesting, roosting and "loafing" birds.
The Bird Hazard Management Plan shall be implemented as approved and shall remain in force for the life of the building. No subsequent alterations to the plan are to take place unless first submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.
Supporting notes:
The Bird Hazard Management Plan must ensure that flat/shallow pitched roofs be constructed to allow access to all areas by foot using permanent fixed access stairs ladders or similar. The owner/occupier must not allow gulls, to nest, roost or loaf on the building. Checks must be made weekly or sooner if bird activity dictates, during the breeding season. Outside of the breeding season gull activity must be monitored and the roof checked regularly to ensure that gulls do not utilise the roof. Any gulls found nesting, roosting or loafing must be dispersed by the owner/occupier when detected or when requested by Heathrow Airside Operations staff. In some instances, it may be necessary to contact Heathrow Airside Operations staff before bird dispersal takes place. The owner/occupier must remove any nests or eggs found on the roof.
The breeding season for gulls typically runs from March to June. The owner/occupier must obtain the appropriate licences where applicable from Natural England before the removal of nests and eggs.
Condition : 29 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am to 6:00pm on Mondays to Friday and 8:00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority, unless otherwise agreed in writing in advance with the Council. Additionally, HGV deliveries to site during the course of construction will be restricted to 9.30am and 3.00pm on Mondays to Friday, and 9.30am to 1.00pm on Saturdays, and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of the locality and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the public highway.
Condition : 30 - No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) that conforms to current TfL and CLOCS guidance has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The Plan shall include: 
i.	a site plan (showing the areas set out below);
ii.	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage to the adjoining public highway which has been caused directly by the development hereby permitted (including demolition and construction phases); 
iii.	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors, and any interim car parking measures that might be necessary during the construction period;
iv.	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
v.	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
vi.	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network (including hours of access, access and egress arrangements within the site and security procedures);
vii.	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate, and clear contact details of the site manager;
viii.	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
ix.	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works;

The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review.
